acme_integration: hey team, we rolled traffic to the canary at ~14:07 UTC and our ingest pipeline suddenly started receiving objects with missing required keys (order_id) and items set to null. This is breaking our downstream parser. sample request_id: rq_0a9f2c. Can you help?
jamie_cs: sorry to hear that — can you paste a sample input + the model's raw output (JSON) you got back?
acme_integration: sending minimal repro: prompt was a shopify order parsing prompt. expected schema includes order_id (string), customer {name,email}, items [ {id,qty} ]
acme_integration: ```json
# expected (what our parser expects)
{
  "order_id": "ORD-12345",
  "customer": {"name":"A. Buyer","email":"a@example.com"},
  "items": [{"id":"SKU-1","qty":2}]
}
```
acme_integration: ```json
# actual response (from model)
{
  "order_id": null,
  "customer": {"name":"A. Buyer","email":"a@example.com"},
  "items": null
}
```
acme_integration: we only started seeing this after the canary flip (traffic 10% -> 50%). Prior baseline had correct JSON.
jamie_cs: thanks — that looks like required keys became nullified. Are you using structured_output_strict or schema enforcement on your client side?
acme_integration: we rely on model to produce those keys (we run a lightweight validator post-response). No strict enforcement on our side.
mira_ml: tagging in — which model was the canary using? any quantized variant?
acme_integration: model in canary: redwood-3.2-small-int8 (traffic=50% at 14:07). Baseline was redwood-3.2-small-fp16.
mira_ml: hmm int8 variant could change tokenization/behavior. Can you share full request headers + request_id and approximate prompt length?
acme_integration: request_id rq_0a9f2c, prompt length ~320 tokens. sending headers in DM.
sam_prod_eng: @mira_ml @alex_sre I see a deploy event tied to that canary: deploy_bot reported canary rollout to redwood-3.2-small-int8 at 2026-03-12T14:05:42Z. rolling back is an option if this is widespread.
deploy_bot: canary deploy: service=runtime, canary_id=canary-20260312-7, model=redwood-3.2-small-int8, traffic=50% -> started at 2026-03-12T14:05:42Z
alex_sre: grabbing logs for rq_0a9f2c. Any chance the client is post-processing (stringifying) or truncating?
acme_integration: not doing any postprocessing besides trimming whitespace. We validated preflight.
mira_ml: do we have other customers reporting similar nullified required fields?
jamie_cs: not yet on the CS side, this is the first customer report.
sam_prod_eng: quick check: int8 model was last tuned with a different JSON template for structured_output which may have been shorter. Possibly model learned a token that maps to empty/null for some schema roots.
mira_ml: can you run a controlled repro using the canary model via API with the same prompt and include stream logs? If you can't, we can repro internally.
acme_integration: we can test — will run a call and paste response. Give us 10m.
acme_integration: (10m later) ran test with canary directly, got same nulls. Sent full response + raw tokens to jamie_cs DM.
jamie_cs: received. escalating to ML lead. @mira_ml can you confirm severity and recommended action?
mira_ml: severity: high for structured-output customers. Root cause hypothesis: quantization-induced token probability shifts causing model to emit JSON value tokens like null (or empty token) for those fields under this prompt template. Next steps: 1) reproduce internally with same seed + prompt, 2) test with fp16 baseline, 3) if repro, rollback canary and mark model variant as incompatible for structured_output_strict use cases.
sam_prod_eng: I'll prepare rollback plan to cut traffic back to baseline 100% if we confirm repro.
alex_sre: collected logs show similar pattern: thousands of responses in the canary window with items=null when prompt contains list of product lines.
jamie_cs: opened ticket CS-4821 and notified account team. @acme_integration apologies — we're treating this as high priority.
acme_integration: thanks. ETA on rollback? This is failing our nightly ingest jobs.
sam_prod_eng: aiming for rollback in 45m if internal repro confirms. Will keep you posted in this thread.
mira_ml: also adding a short-term mitigation: we can apply a server-side postprocessing step to rehydrate missing arrays if safe (but that's a hack). Prefer rollback.
jamie_cs: noted. I've provided customer with temporary ingestion workaround: if items==null, reject and queue for manual fallback route.
acme_integration: ok will implement fallback. keep us posted. :handshake:
sam_prod_eng: internal repro complete — fp16 baseline returns correct keys; int8 canary reproduces null items/order_id. Initiating rollback now.
deploy_bot: rollback initiated: canary_id=canary-20260312-7 -> traffic set to 0%. baseline restored to redwood-3.2-small-fp16.
jamie_cs: rollback complete 14:54 UTC. @acme_integration can you confirm if recent requests look normal?
acme_integration: ran tests after rollback — responses look correct now. order_id and items present. thanks everyone.
mira_ml: follow-ups: 1) block redwood-3.2-small-int8 from structured-output experiments until we retrain/regtest with schema prompts, 2) add regression tests that run canonical schema prompts across quantized variants, 3) add telemetry to track nullified required keys per model variant.
sam_prod_eng: created follow-up infra ticket INF-719 to add model-variant schema regression job.
jamie_cs: closing loop with ACME and logging postmortem entry.
acme_integration: appreciate the quick response. please share postmortem when available.
jamie_cs: will do — thanks team. :thumbsup:
